## Question 2 [15 points]

In the area marked as `???` write a regular expression that accomplishes the requested task. Use the `strings` object to demonstrate your answer is correct by giving a minimum of two TRUE and two FALSE responses. **Be sure to change the chunk option to eval=TRUE.**

**a.** [7 points] An expression that can determine if a string contains any of the following words: `Alpha`, `Bravo`, `Delta`, `Echo`, `Foxtrot`.

```{r}
### Change to eval=TRUE or remove eval option
strings <- c('Alpha', 'Bravo', 'Delta', 'Echo', 'Foxtrot')
data.frame( string = strings ) %>%
  mutate( result = str_detect(string, 'a') )
```

**b.** [8 points] An expression that can determine if a string starts with exactly three letters (any upper or lowercase), followed by a dash, followed by exactly four digits, with nothing after. For example, `ABC-1234` should be TRUE, but `ABC-12345` should be FALSE.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
### Change to eval=TRUE or remove eval option
strings <- c('ABC-1234','ABA-1234', 'ABC-12345','Aaa-1')
data.frame( string = strings ) %>%
  mutate( result = str_detect(string,'([a-zA-Z]{3})-([0-9]{4})'))
```

## Question 3 [15 points]

The required timezone information is provided in each question! Answer the following date-time questions.

**a.** [5 points] A video call is scheduled to start at 3:00 PM local time on March 10th, 2026 in `America/New_York`.  Create the object `Call.Start` for this time stamp, be sure to include the timezone. Display the object to screen.

```{r}
Call.Start<- mdy_hm('March 10, 2026 3:00 PM', tz='America/New_york')
Call.Start
```

**b.** [5 points] What time will it be in `US/Arizona` when the call starts?  Return/display the results of an R calculation here.

```{r}
with_tz(Call.Start, tz='US/Arizona')
```

**c.** [5 points] The call lasts $90$ minutes. Create the object `Call.End` using an R calculation on `Call.Start`, and then display what the date and time will be in `Asia/Tokyo` when the call ends.

```{r}
Call.End <- Call.Start- minutes(90)
with_tz(Call.End, tz= 'Asia/Tokyo')
```

## Question 4 [35 points]

The `Exam1_Data_F26.xlsx` file contains data developed across two field survey trips (`ID`). Information was collected at four different `Sites` during four different `Periods` of the day. Two counts were taken for each observation and were recorded as `Birds` and `Insects`. There are potentially many observations of the same `Period` and `Site`. The data from the two trips is available on Sheets 2 and 3 of the provided file. Sheet 4 contains information about each of the four sites. 

**a.** [7 points] Read in the two different data sets on Sheets 2 and 3. Row bind the data into a single data frame named `Q4data`. There should be 5 columns: `ID`, `Site`, `Period`, `Birds`, `Insects`, totaling 100 observations. Demonstrate this by returning to screen the structure of the `Q4data` object. This can be done using the `str()` function. Do __not__ display any of the data.frames in your final answer, only the structure of the combined data frame (a tibble is acceptable).

```{r}
Sheet_2 <- read_excel("../data-raw/Exam1_Data_F26.xlsx", sheet=2)
Sheet_3 <- read_excel("../data-raw/Exam1_Data_F26.xlsx", sheet=3)
Q4data <- rbind(Sheet_2,Sheet_3)
str(Q4data)
```

**b.** [5 points] Read in the site information on Sheet 4. **Join** this information onto `Q4data` so that every observation also has the `Elevation_m` and `Canopy` of its `Site`. Save the result as `Q4join` and display the `head`.

```{r}
Sheet_4 <- read_excel("../data-raw/Exam1_Data_F26.xlsx", sheet=4)
Q4join<- inner_join(Q4data,Sheet_4)
head(Q4join)
```
